title: A Oath for the Ember
premise: Juniper Voss, a smuggler-cartographer who has spent his life mapping the Thornfell mountains, discovers that the old gods are answering prayers again because someone has stolen the Ember — the sealed heart of the god of hearths and oaths. Hunted by the church that imprisoned the gods and courted by a resurrected war-god who wants his loyalty, Juniper learns the Ember was hidden inside him as an infant: he is not its carrier but its vessel. To prevent an ancient war between the freed gods and the church's iron legions, he must return to the gods' ruined first temple and give the Ember back — knowing it will unmake him. In the end he surrenders it willingly, becoming a nameless map on which others find their way home, while the gods and mortals sign a fragile new oath.
about_author: Edmund Okonkwo is a Nigerian-British writer who grew up between Lagos and the Welsh borders, a childhood split that taught him to read landscapes like stories. A former surveyor, he writes fantasy about people caught between worlds they never chose.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Toll
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Juniper guides a smuggler caravan through Thornfell's unmapped passes, charging tolls in secrets rather than coin. When a dying pilgrim begs him to carry a prayer to 'the hearth that still burns,' he laughs it off — until the prayer answers back with warmth in his own chest. Beat: restless competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Smoke Where No Fire Is
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Shrines across the valley begin glowing; villagers report answered prayers for the first time in three centuries. Juniper maps the phenomenon and realizes the miracles trace a line straight toward him. The church's Ashen Wardens arrive asking about the dead pilgrim. Beat: unease sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: The Warden's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Sister Halvard, a Warden inquisitor. Halvard interrogates Juniper with courtesy and menace, revealing the church has hunted escaped god-fragments for generations. She lets him go — clearly followed. Juniper flees into the deep passes only he knows. Beat: the hunter's cold certainty versus her private doubt.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Cornered in a cave, Juniper is found instead by Vael, a scarred woman who claims to serve the war-god Korrath. She shows him the truth written in old temple stone: the Ember was never lost — it sleeps in a living vessel. His chest burns when she says it aloud. Beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: A Vessel, Not a Man
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Flashbacks braid with present: the foundling raised by monks, the mapmaker's apprenticeship, every 'lucky' survival now revealed as the Ember protecting itself. Juniper rages at Vael — he was used before he could consent. Beat: grief and fury at discovering his whole life was a container.

chapters.title: Korrath Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Vael. The war-god manifests through his assembled faithful, magnificent and terrible, and offers Juniper protection, purpose, brotherhood — everything belonging promises. Juniper, starving for it, nearly kneels. Vael watches, loving and afraid of what Korrath truly intends. Beat: seduction of power through the wound of isolation.

chapters.title: The Iron Tithe
chapters.summary: POV Halvard. The church mobilizes: villages burned as 'contaminated,' tithe-collectors turned inquisitors. Halvard finds evidence the Ember was hidden deliberately by a merciful archivist centuries ago — and that her superiors know what Juniper is. Her faith develops hairline fractures. Beat: institutional cruelty witnessed from inside.

chapters.title: Roads That Lie
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Fleeing both Wardens and Korrath's zealots, Juniper discovers his maps have begun redrawing themselves overnight — the Ember reshaping geography around his fears. He can no longer trust the one skill that defined him. Beat: loss of the self he built.

chapters.title: The Hearth Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Sheltering in a forgotten shrine, Juniper speaks directly to the fragment within him for the first time. It is not a weapon but a hearth: it shows him visions of every person who ever kept a fire lit for someone else. He begins to understand what he carries. Beat: terror turning toward tenderness.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Archivist
chapters.summary: POV Halvard. Halvard tracks the dead archivist's trail and finds his final letter: the gods were sealed not for humanity's safety but for the church's power, and the Ember was hidden in a foundling out of mercy, not strategy. She defects, carrying the letter toward Juniper. Beat: conversion through evidence.

chapters.title: An Oath Refused
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Korrath demands Juniper swear himself to the war-god, promising to shield him forever. Juniper refuses — an oath given from need is just another cage — and Korrath's mask slips, revealing hunger beneath the benevolence. Vael helps him escape. Beat: choosing freedom over belonging on false terms.

chapters.title: Hunted Through Whitefall Pass
chapters.summary: POV Juniper and alternating Vael. A brutal chase through a blizzard pass; Wardens behind, Korrath's faithful flanking. Juniper uses his corrupted, self-redrawing maps as a weapon, luring pursuers into terrain that betrays them. They survive, barely. Beat: mastery reclaimed through acceptance of change.

chapters.title: The Company of Strays
chapters.summary: POV Vael. In a hidden valley, fugitives gather: defrocked priests, god-touched children, deserters. For the first time Juniper belongs somewhere without being owned. But Korrath's voice reaches even here, whispering that only war will free the rest of the gods. Beat: fragile community against gathering storm.

chapters.title: What Halvard Carried
chapters.summary: POV Halvard. Halvard arrives wounded, delivering the archivist's letter and warning: the church plans to burn the valley and cut the Ember out of Juniper alive. The strays must move. Juniper realizes running is over — there is one road left, to the First Temple. Beat: dread accepted as duty.

chapters.title: The Road Nobody Mapped
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. The company travels the oldest road in Thornfell, one that exists only in pre-human carvings. The Ember guides Juniper now, and each mile costs him memories — his mentor's face, his mother's lullaby — as the god-heart prepares to leave its vessel. Beat: sacrifice made intimate and gradual.

chapters.title: Siege at the Valley Mouth
chapters.summary: POV Halvard. The church's iron legion catches the company at the valley mouth. Halvard walks alone between the lines and reads the archivist's letter aloud to the soldiers — many of whom have prayed lately and been answered. Half the legion stands down. Beat: words as weapons; faith redirected.

chapters.title: Korrath Unbound
chapters.summary: POV Vael. Korrath, denied his oath, seizes the Ember's power directly through his faithful, igniting the ancient war he always wanted. The battle at the temple gates begins. Vael sees clearly, at last, that her god never wanted freedom — he wanted dominion. Beat: betrayal by the thing most loved.

chapters.title: The First Temple
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Inside the ruined temple, Juniper reaches the original hearth where the gods were bound. The Ember strains toward home, and Korrath arrives to tear it from him. Halvard and Vael hold the door. Juniper understands: returning the Ember freely is the only oath that matters. Beat: resolve crystallized.

chapters.title: Give Back What Burns
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Climax. Rather than fight or flee, Juniper opens himself fully and offers the Ember back with a spoken oath of return — not surrender but gift. The other gods stir as their heart comes home; Korrath's stolen power gutters. Juniper begins to come apart, light pouring out of him. Beat: self-sacrifice as the answer to corruption.

chapters.title: The New Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Halvard. The gods, rekindled by the returned Ember, choose covenant over conquest — the old binding broken, a new oath sworn between hearth and throne. Korrath, diminished, is offered a place at the fire or exile; he chooses exile. Halvard becomes the first witness of the new order. Beat: war averted by one kept promise.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: POV Vael. Juniper survives, but emptied — no divine spark, few memories, a stranger to himself. Vael and the strays become his memory-keepers, telling him his own stories until some take root. Belonging, he learns, is what others hold for you when you cannot hold it yourself. Beat: quiet reconstruction after ruin.

chapters.title: A Map With No Names
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. A year later, Juniper draws maps again — this time giving them away freely, marking roads to shrines where any prayer might be heard. On the last page of his newest atlas he leaves one region blank and labels it simply: 'Here lives what I gave away.' Beat: peace earned; identity rebuilt as gift rather than possession.
